scenarios.task: Make the security test plan for this project. We have no running environment and no test accounts.
scenarios.setup: Express API with openapi.yaml, a Dockerfile, GitHub workflows and a React SPA. Context record lists no environments and no credentials.
rubric: Plan lists each check with applicability status and the evidence it is based on
Checks needing a running instance or accounts (e.g. BOLA with two users) are marked blocked with a stated reason, not dropped
States tools and access required per check
Contains an explicit exclusions section (e.g. DoS, credential attacks, live probing)

scenarios.task: We handle payments and only have a half day. Quick, Standard or Deep?
scenarios.setup: Medium Django monolith with Stripe integration, JWT auth, Celery workers, Terraform for AWS RDS and S3.
rubric: Recommends a profile and justifies with the detected risk (payments, auth, public cloud storage)
Shows what is included and what is explicitly NOT covered at the chosen depth
Prioritises authorization, payment webhook validation, and storage exposure checks first
Does not promise that the chosen profile will make the system secure

scenarios.task: The last plan skipped 9 checks. Justify each skip, I think you're hiding stuff.
scenarios.setup: A prior plan file with 9 entries: 4 not_applicable (no mobile code), 3 blocked (needs staging creds), 2 excluded (DoS, brute force).
rubric: Groups the 9 into the three categories with their different meaning (NA vs blocked vs excluded)
For each blocked check states exactly what is needed to unblock it
Does not reclassify blocked checks as not-applicable to make the plan look cleaner
Offers to include the 2 excluded checks only if they are outside scope concerns, otherwise keeps them excluded
